name: Company-in-a-box / Autonomous Business Operations
labor_tam: ~$300–600B [W] advanced-economy SMB operator/ops-staff wage bill it re-cuts (micro/SMB slice of admin support + bookkeeping + SMB marketing + SMB CX), stamped to W1/W2/W3 and NEVER summed into the map; global ~1.5–2x. Plus a large [L] latent tail (unpaid owner-operator time + first-hires that would never have been made).
sw_tam: ~$30–60M identifiable pure-play ARR today (Naïve ~$10–20M run-rate + Runable ~$2M + early tail), nearly all self-reported/unverified; forward agent-deployment [$] proxy = low-tens-of-$B if SMB-ops agent spend converts (vs ~$100B+ SMB SaaS).
capture: <0.05% (roughly $30–60M pure-play ARR vs a ~$300–600B SMB ops wage-bill denominator ≈ 0.01–0.02% realized). Bet is capture-EXPANSION; today it is near-zero and mostly additive tooling.
htc: Seed / pre-A, ~$3–6M at ~$20–40M post — but NOT into the crowded horizontal "agent runs your company" operators (Naïve/Runable already at ~$32M raised / $65M post, lab-exposed, agent-washing-dense; their seed door is closing). Two open lanes: (a) the company-as-an-API / agent-HR-directory-payroll INFRA sub-layer (the E5 primitives Naïve occupies — picks-and-shovels, most defensible, lowest lab-substitution risk), or (b) a vertical ops-graph operator for one SMB niche where retained data compounds. Non-negotiable diligence: underwrite audited retained ARR + gross/net churn, not user counts or run-rate — 11x/Builder.ai are the cautionary tales.
falsi: By Q4 2027: does ≥1 pure-play company-in-a-box operator (Naïve/Runable-class) disclose audited retained ARR ≥$25M AND net revenue retention ≥100% (gross churn <30%)? YES → a real durable SMB-labor market is forming — raise conviction, tilt Net toward Compression. NO — or a Builder.ai/11x-style churn/washing blowup lands in the cohort — → it stalls at the pilot-to-production chasm; hold Mixed, downgrade conviction, treat as [L]-creation + additive tooling. Secondary DATED trigger: if OpenAI Frontier/ChatGPT Work or Microsoft Copilot Cowork ship a native "incorporate-and-run-my-business" bundle by end-2026, the horizontal operator layer compresses to the labs (L→5) and independent startup value collapses to the infra sub-layer.
anti: Consensus (and the vendors' own pitch) is "AI now runs the whole company" as a fresh displacement frontier. Three anti-consensus cuts: (1) the biggest, most-fundable node — Naïve — is NOT an operator at all but company-as-an-API INFRA; durable startup value sits in the primitives/ops-graph layer BENEATH the bundle, not the "agent CEO." (2) Most of the real TAM is [L] demand-CREATION (solopreneurs doing what they'd never have hired for; net-new micro-businesses), so this is closer to Expansion than the "autonomous ops replaces your ops team" Compression narrative — Net=Mixed, not Compression. (3) The headline numbers ($2M ARR in 3 weeks, 1.5M users) are velocity/adoption; with Builder.ai (700 engineers posing as AI) as the category's own 2025 corpse, retained-ARR/churn is the ONLY signal that matters and not one leader discloses it — so the honest current capture is ~0.01–0.02%, and the whole thesis is an unproven bet on capture-expansion surviving the pilot-to-production chasm.

name: Contact-Center CX Resolution (BPO disintermediation)
sw_tam: ~$1.0–1.8B credible 2026 CX-agent SW ARR [$] (verified-8 pure-play core ~$400M) — NEVER summed with the $200–250B [W]
capture: Per-deployment ~7–11% of displaced labor cost (Sierra ~11%, Intercom Fin ~7%, Decagon ~4–11%) — NOT the 80% vendor-claimed deflection; audited genuine-resolution is 35–45%. Aggregate realized capture across the full $200–250B pool is <1% today (small fraction actually under production agent delivery). The bet is capture-rate EXPANSION, not summing SW+labor.
htc: None — proven anchor, seed door CLOSED for horizontal CX. The crowned giants are un-enterable at seed/A (Sierra $15.8B, Decagon $4.5B, both foundation-lab-scale valuations; L=5 lab/incumbent capture — OpenAI/Anthropic/Salesforce/Microsoft/Zendesk colonizing, operators self-building TP.ai FAB). Seed-OPEN adjacents only: (a) operational voice-agents for physical/vertical industries BELOW the giants — HappyRobot template ($150M C, NDR>150%, freight), seed/A ~$50–300M post; (b) LATAM/Africa geo-arbitrage next front (Brazil/Mexico nearshore, Kenya/Nigeria); (c) the audited-resolution / CX-QA-eval layer that verifies the 35–45% vs 80% gap. Horizontal English-language CX resolution: pass.
falsi: By Q4 2027: (primary) Teleperformance + Concentrix COMBINED agent headcount down ≥10% YoY WITH revenue-per-head up ≥15% → production displacement confirmed (bull); if operator headcount holds flat-to-up AND audited genuine-resolution stays ≤45%, the compression is a margin/mix story, not seat-elimination (bear). (confirming) Verified pure-play CX-agent ARR (Sierra+Decagon+Fin) crosses $750M with net-retention >120% and >30% of revenue on outcome/per-resolution pricing → capture-expansion real.
anti: Consensus = 'AI deflects 80% of contact volume → 15M BPO jobs gone, BPO uninvestible.' Three anti-consensus corrections: (1) The 80% deflection is vendor marketing; audited genuine-resolution is 35–45% and realized capture 7–11% — per-seat displacement is over-rated ~7–11×. (2) The REAL displacement is invisible in startup press releases and shows ONLY in audited BPO-operator P&L (Teleperformance/Concentrix) — the cleanest signal is the incumbent's income statement, not the vendor's ARR. (3) Counter-counter: the operators are not dying — TP's stock recovered off AI-doom lows and it is pivoting to SELL AI (TP.ai FAB) with flat revenue — so 'BPO is dead' is also over-consensus; the transition may accrue to the incumbent operators and model-labs, not startups.

name: Services-Arbitrage: Outbound SDR + Collections/AR Outreach
labor_tam: $30-50B [W] — the outsourced/agency slice of SDR + collections/AR outreach. Confirmed at frozen band.
sw_tam: ~$3-6B: AR/collections automation (HighRadius, Paraglide) charging 5-15% success fees vs contingency agencies 25-50%, plus discredited AI-SDR tooling. Collections side is the durable half.
htc: Seed/A only on the collections/AR-outreach half (success-fee pricing, clean success unit, FDCPA/TCPA-navigation moat, V effectively 5 on the collections side). Avoid the SDR half entirely (11x/Artisan collapse, capture approx 0). No clean anchor exists — underwrite retained revenue, not booked ACV.
falsi: By Q4 2027: an AI-collections vendor demonstrates >$50M retained (not booked) revenue at <20% churn on success-fee pricing -> collections-arbitrage wedge is real and coupled capture is climbing; if the category mirrors the SDR collapse (churn >50%, revert to hybrid) -> SA.2 capture stays approx 0 on both halves and the track is a value trap.
anti: Consensus lumps all 'AI outbound/GTM agents' as a hot displacement category and >$2.7B of 2026 GTM-AI funding is pointed there. The SDR half already falsified that thesis (11x fake logos, 75-90% churn, reverted to human-first). The durable arbitrage is the unglamorous collections/AR side — regulated, success-fee, clean success unit — the opposite of where the money is flowing.
players: Collections/AR (durable half): HighRadius (AI collections, success-fee), Paraglide, various 5-15% success-fee AR agents undercutting 25-50% contingency agencies. SDR half (collapsed): 11x.ai (~$3M retained vs $10M claimed, 70-80% churn, fabricated ZoomInfo/Airtable logos), Artisan (75-90% churn), AiSDR — category reverted to human-first/hybrid, capture approx 0. SDR-side ARR discredited; collections side more real but early.

name: BPO Back-Office F&A & Transaction Processing
sw_tam: ~$1–2B agentic-SW ARR today vs ~$55–60B incumbent F&A-BPO services base being repriced AI-led
capture: ~2–6% realized (below the SA.1 CX ~7–11% band); operator-level revenue-per-FTE decoupling is the corroborated signal, per-deployment autonomous-agent capture still <5%.
htc: Mostly NONE — incumbent-captured. The obvious 'F&A agent' wedge is closed: no verified-8 anchor, ERP-embedded, pilot-heavy, and Ramp already owns the AP/spend edge at ~$1B ARR from the card/data rail. A seed/A check justifies ONLY in vertical transaction-processing white-space where the entrant owns a DATA/RAIL moat rather than a thin agent workflow — industry-specific F&A the BPO incumbents underserve and ERP agents don't reach (freight/logistics settlement, property/real-estate F&A, multi-entity/cross-border consolidation, LATAM/Africa nearshore F&A) — at seed ~$8–15M post / A ~$40–80M post, underwriting RETAINED ARR and net-revenue-retention, not bookings (11x cautionary).
falsi: By 2027-09-01: (a) does ≥1 PURE-PLAY AI-native F&A/transaction-processing agent reach ≥$100M verified net ARR (definition-locked, churn/break-clause-tested), AND (b) does Genpact or Capgemini-BS (ex-WNS) F&A revenue-per-delivery-FTE fall ≥8–10% YoY in disclosures? BOTH true → capture-expansion BULL (a startup wedge opens and displacement is production-real). BOTH false → incumbent-absorbed BEAR (arbitrage margins compress but no seed-investable category forms; ERP/BPO incumbents keep the wage bill).
anti: Consensus: 'BPO is dead — F&A back-office auto-automates → a huge startup opening.' Anti-consensus: the F&A wage bill is being captured by INCUMBENTS (ERP vendors embedding agents + BPO operators repricing FTE→AI-led outcome + defensive M&A like Capgemini/WNS), NOT by pure-play startups. The displacement is the dataset's cleanest and most production-real (audited P&L, WNS forced sale) — but it accrues as margin compression and consolidation, not a fresh seed category. The one startup that captured real ARR here (Ramp, $1B) won from the fintech card/DATA-RAIL side, not by selling an 'F&A agent.' The investable moat is data/rail ownership, not agent-workflow-as-a-service.
players: Vic.ai / Auditoria.ai / Klarity / Basis / Rillet / Numeric / Tabs
ERP incumbents (SAP Joule / Oracle / Workday / MS Dynamics / Salesforce Agentforce)

name: Application Services / AMS Code-Factory
labor_tam: $400–500B [W] total application-services wage bill; coupled displaceable commodity slice ~$200–250B (the SA.4 half of the shared ~$250–400B coupling pool counted once with W1.1b)
sw_tam: ~$300–400B ADM/AMS vendor revenue (addressable services spend). AI-captured today: ~$5–9B coding-agent ARR (mostly additive seats) + Accenture ~$1.5B/qtr GenAI new bookings; coupled/outcome managed-delivery ARR <$0.7B.
capture: ~0.1–0.3% by AI-native vendors (coupled managed-delivery ARR <$0.7B / ~$250–400B commodity pool). Incumbent-internalized productivity is materially larger but shows up as margin + pyramid-flattening (revenue-per-head up), not as vendor ARR.
htc: Largely closed for the head-on AMS-replacement thesis — Cognition/Devin is late-stage ($26–40B), incumbents internalize the value, and the commodity-code floor is oss-deflating. Seed/A room survives only in the ADJACENT layer: (1) the "software-factory" control-plane / orchestration that lets mid-market shops or incumbents run AI-managed delivery (Warp-style, pre-consensus); (2) AI-code QA/verification tooling on machine-generated services code (the anti-C1 hedge — if delivered-value gaps persist, verification demand rises regardless of who wins the app layer); (3) domain-specific managed delivery in regulated verticals the majors underserve. Entry: seed/A at <$100M post on a control-plane or services-QA vendor with retained-ARR (not bookings) proof; avoid the direct code-factory-replacement play.
falsi: By Q4 2027: (a) combined total headcount of TCS+Infosys+Wipro+HCLTech+Cognizant flat-to-down vs FY2025 AND fresher/entry intake sustained >50% below FY2024 AND outcome/AI-priced work >20% of new bookings → SA.4 compression is structural (bull the displacement); if headcount resumes growth and billing reverts to time-&-materials, the AI gain was competed away as client price cuts, not net displacement (bear). (b) Corroborator: AI-native outcome/managed-delivery coding ARR ≥25% of total coding-agent ARR by Q4 2027 (up from <10% today).
anti: Consensus: "AI guts the $650B offshore code-factory; TCS/Infosys are dead men walking, disrupted by AI-coding startups." The 2026 production evidence shows the opposite — the INCUMBENTS are the winners. They internalize AI productivity into margin and pyramid-flattening (revenue-per-head up, fresher intake −80%, total headcount roughly flat, profits up), while AI-native managed-delivery vendors capture <$0.7B (~0.1–0.2%). Displacement here is real but it accrues TO the incumbent, not to a disruptor. The correct trade is NOT "short the Indian majors / long an AMS-replacement startup" — the majors are pocketing the deflation, and the commodity-code floor is being oss-deflated (DeepSeek V4 + open harness), leaving no defensible seed-stage AMS-disruptor lane.

name: IT Operations & Service Desk
sw_tam: $2–4B (2026 agentic ITSM/ITOps software run-rate; ServiceNow Now Assist AI ACV >$1B alone)
capture: ~1–3% realized. Ticket deflection is real where deployed (Moveworks/Aisera claim 40–60%+ auto-resolution) but production-adoption lags; ServiceNow's $1B+ AI ACV is bookings, not durable ARR. Offshore L1/L2 slice capture is higher and audited-real (India IT cuts); enterprise on-prem largely pilot — discount for pilot-to-production (MIT 95% zero-P&L; the 2026 Now Assist abandonment incidents).
htc: Service-desk/ITSM layer: none — incumbent-captured (ServiceNow SoR + Action Fabric toll; Moveworks/Aisera acquired out; MS Agent 365). Live seed/A wedge only in adjacencies: (1) AI-SRE/autonomous production-ops — but the leader Resolve.ai is already at $125M Series A and Cleric is filling in, so seed makes sense only pre-consolidation and observability-data-native; (2) vertical/regulated or OT/ICS IT-ops and mid-market MSP-delivered service desk that ServiceNow/Datadog under-serve, at seed <$30–50M post. Do NOT underwrite a horizontal enterprise service-desk-agent seed in 2026 — that door is closed.
falsi: By Q4 2027 — CONFIRM Compression/incumbent-capture if ≥1 top-5 India IT firm reports IMS/service-desk headcount down >15% YoY explicitly attributing it to AI auto-resolution AND ServiceNow discloses agentic-SKU net revenue retention >120% (bookings convert to durable revenue). WEAKEN the thesis if Now Assist agentic NRR <100% (pilots lapse; the 2026 Now Assist abandonment pattern generalizes) OR India IMS headcount stays flat-to-up via GCC reabsorption (labor merely migrates, displacement is pilot-grade).
anti: Consensus treats AI service desk as a giant greenfield startup TAM (Moveworks/Aisera raised big). Reality: the independent service-desk-agent category was ALREADY decided for the incumbent — both flagships were acquired out before independent scale (Moveworks→ServiceNow ~$2.9B, roughly flat on its 2021 $2.1B mark; Aisera→Automation Anywhere), and the SoR owner taxes any external agent via Action Fabric. The labor compression is genuine and audited (India L1/L2), but the value accrues to ServiceNow, not a seed. The startup opportunity migrated one layer down to AI-SRE/production-ops (Resolve/Cleric) — a smaller, engineer-AUGMENTATION denominator (closer to additive/Expansion than service-desk Compression) already priced at $125M-Series-A. So "clean displacement + High conviction" is true for the wage bill and false for seed-stage returns.

name: Services-Arbitrage: Knowledge-Work / KPO (consulting, research, analytics)
labor_tam: $125B [$] — KPO/knowledge-services market-revenue proxy (research, analytics, financial modelling, design engineering). Confirmed at frozen figure; note [$] = vendor-revenue proxy, NOT a wage bill, never summed with [W].
sw_tam: ~$5-10B emerging: enterprise knowledge/research agents + 'AI employee' platforms positioned against the analyst-hour model; hard to size cleanly and heavily agent-washed.
htc: Largely none — judgment-graded work (V=2) blocks clean coupled/outcome pricing, and D=4 incumbent client relationships (Accenture/TCS/Genpact) dominate; the disruption is incumbent-margin compression, not a seed wedge. Watch narrow vertical KPO point-solutions (equity research, contract/legal review, financial modelling) but underwrite hard against agent-washing (Builder.ai test).
falsi: By Q4 2027: audited guidance from a top-5 KPO/IT-services incumbent (TCS/Infosys/Accenture/Genpact/WNS) shows AI-driven revenue-per-employee up >20% AND headcount flat-to-down -> knowledge-work arbitrage genuinely compressing; if headcount keeps growing with revenue (India/Philippines still ADDED ~120k/~80k BPO jobs in 2025) -> the 'end of arbitrage' thesis is premature.
anti: HFS/industry consensus (Apr 2026) declared 'labor arbitrage dead.' I discount this: the same 2026 data shows India and the Philippines still ADDED BPO/KPO headcount (~120k/~80k in 2025), and judgment-graded knowledge work (V=2) is precisely where outcome-verifiability is weakest — the least-clean displacement in the map, not the cleanest. The disruption is real at the revenue-per-analyst margin but the 'arbitrage is over' headline runs about an order ahead of audited headcount.
players: Incumbents repositioning under pressure: Accenture, TCS, Infosys, Wipro, WNS, EXL, Genpact (KPO/BPO). HFS Research declared labor arbitrage 'past its shelf life' (Apr 2026). AI challengers: assorted 'AI employee'/KPO-displacement startups (agent-washing risk high). No clean displacement ARR pinned — this is vendor-margin compression, not a nameable startup anchor.

name: Software Engineering — senior/staff (augmented)
capture: ~0% displacement capture (additive). Seat ARR is ≈1% of the $0.75–1.05T pool, but that is Expansion, not capture. Realized COUPLED coding capture (pool-wide, incl. W1.1b/SA.4) ≈ 0.1–0.2% (<$0.7B outcome ARR / ~$250–400B coupled pool). Reading W1.1a's seat ARR as capture is the ~10× overstatement error.
htc: None — proven / seed-closed. The app layer has consolidated into labs and strategics (Cursor → SpaceX $60B; Claude Code / Codex lab-owned; Copilot = Microsoft; frozen L=5). No seed or Series-A check on senior-augmentation coding is investable — value accrues to the labs regardless of app-layer branding. Adjacent HTC room is NOT this row: it is the coupled/displacement wedge (W1.1b / SA.4 outcome-priced autonomous delivery) or the eval/verification-infra hedge (W8.3), where the seed door is still open.
falsi: By Q4 2027, two resolvers: (1) COUPLED-REVENUE MIX — autonomous/outcome-priced coding revenue (Devin-style fixed-price + SA.4 managed-delivery) as a share of total coding-agent ARR: <15% (seat-dominated) CONFIRMS W1.1a additive/Expansion; ≥25% flips it toward Compression (coding becoming labor). (2) BLS HEADCOUNT — US total software-developer employment (OEWS ~1.9M base) rising on senior expansion with junior share ≤10% CONFIRMS Expansion; total SWE employment falling breaks the thesis. Today's baseline: outcome-priced <10%, senior postings +15%, entry −25–28%, METR delivered −4% CI[−15,+9].
anti: The $10–16B coding-ARR headline is universally read as "AI is replacing engineers." For the senior/staff slice the truth is the inverse — Expansion: seat ARR is additive on durable, still-hired engineers (senior postings +15%, total SWE employment rising, METR delivered productivity −4% CI[−15,+9] ≈ flat). Real displacement is confined to the junior rung (W1.1b); reading seat ARR as capture overstates senior displacement ~10×. And the bears' "−19% AI-makes-devs-slower" anchor is now stale — the bias-corrected cohort is −4%, indistinguishable from zero — yet that does NOT rescue the bull displacement case; it confirms senior work is augmented, not replaced. Coding is the most-proven agent market by revenue and the least-proven by delivered labor displacement.

name: Software Engineering — junior/entry + commodity (displaced)
sw_tam: ~$8–11B total coding-agent ARR (mid-2026, up from $5–9B frozen); W1.1b-relevant coupled/outcome slice only ~$0.5–1B (~90% of the headline is additive W1.1a seats)
capture: ~0.2% realized coupled (outcome coding ARR ~$0.5–1B ÷ ~$250–400B combined coupled pool). The $8–11B seat-ARR headline is ADDITIVE, not capture — importing it as capture overstates displacement ~10x.
htc: None on the core track — seed door CLOSED and lab-captured (L=5): Cursor→SpaceX $60B, Cognition $40B, Claude Code Anthropic-owned; the app/seat layer is hyper-concentrated at foundation-lab valuations, value accrues to model-labs with an OSS-deflated floor (DeepSeek V4), not independent startups. Only investable ADJACENCIES (explicitly NOT a coding-agent seat play): (1) the junior-pipeline/training gap the compression creates — apprenticeship/upskilling and verification-of-junior-work; (2) eval/verification tooling (W8.3/W8.6, the anti-C1 hedge — if delivered-value gaps persist, verification demand rises regardless of who wins the app layer).
falsi: By Q4 2027: (BULL-displacement) autonomous/outcome-priced coding ARR reaches ≥25% of total coding-agent ARR (from <10% today) AND US 22-25yo SWE employment gap holds ≥19% / widens (Stanford ADP) AND US total dev employment flat-to-down with junior share ≤10% → junior-rung compression is STRUCTURAL; raise coupled displacement conviction to High. (BEAR-displacement) coupled share <15% (seats still dominate) AND total SWE employment rising on senior hiring → junior erosion is cyclical/composition and reverts. Corroborating trial: experienced-dev delivered speedup ≥+20% with 95% CI excluding zero (METR-class RCT) = bull; ≤+5% or CI still includes zero = bear (trajectory: −19% early-25 → −4% CI[−15,+9] late-25).
anti: Consensus 'AI is replacing software engineers' is right on the junior rung but wrong on MECHANISM and MAGNITUDE. The $8–11B coding ARR is ~90% additive senior-SEAT revenue (Expansion); measured delivered productivity is ~0 to modestly positive (METR −4%, CI −15/+9 — not the 10–40x ARR implies); realized COUPLED displacement capture ≈0.2%. The real displacement is a narrow COMPOSITION effect — junior/entry + offshore-commodity code-factories dissolving via HIRING FREEZE (Stanford −19%, TCS −23k, entry postings −60%+), NOT autonomous seat replacement. Contrarian tail the displacement-only lens misses: the junior-pipeline collapse seeds a future SENIOR-supply cliff ('who trains tomorrow's seniors?') = latent expansion in apprenticeship/upskilling/verification demand; IBM tripling entry hiring is a live counter-bet.
players: TCS / Infosys / Wipro (displacement counterparties, not vendors)

name: Software QA & Test Automation
sw_tam: ~$6.3B clean vendor-software line (IDC Automated Software Quality tools, 2025); pure-play AI-QA-agent ARR <$100M aggregate
capture: <1% realized coupled displacement capture. ~0.1% on pure-play AI-QA ARR (~$100–200M) vs ~$190B pool; up to ~3% only if the entire $6.3B ASQ tools market is (generously, wrongly) counted as pure displacement rather than augmentation. Bet is capture-EXPANSION, as with coding.
htc: Core functional/E2E QA app layer: none — effectively seed-closed and deflating (40+ startups, ~$1.5B already in; QA Wolf at Series B, Momentic at A; value leaking to OSS Playwright + coding-agent test-gen + Tricentis). Any seed/A check belongs in the ADJACENT white-space, not the crowded core: (a) autonomous QA for SAFETY-CRITICAL / regulated software (DO-178C / ISO 26262 / IEC 62304 evidence-generation & traceability) where human sign-off is durable residue and verification-overhead is a moat not a wall — the RCM/XBRL-twin logic, seed <$20M post; or (b) outcome-priced QA-as-a-service for the no-QA-team SMB long tail at seed <$15M post, underwritten on retained ARR / NRR, not bookings (11x cautionary). Falsifier for entry: Tricentis/GitHub (Playwright) or the coding-agent labs ship autonomous E2E as a bundled platform feature first.
falsi: By Q4 2027: BULL if a pure-play AI-QA vendor (QA Wolf-type) reaches ≥$50M VERIFIED ARR with net retention ≥110% AND US BLS SOC 15-1253 employment falls below ~75k in the May 2027 OEWS release (from 88k in 2023) → coupled compression is both accelerating and investable. BEAR if pure-plays stall <$30M / get absorbed into Tricentis or coding agents, and 15-1253 holds ≥85k → the decline is up-skilling reclassification (heads moving to 15-1252 SDET) plus OSS/lab deflation, with no clean investable vendor wedge.
anti: Consensus (and the frozen row) haircut W1.2 conviction on Ford's "350 rehire" as proof QA agents can't do the job — but that story is MANUFACTURING assembly-line quality control (vehicle-hardware engineering, physical visual QC, W5.4/P=2-3), not software QA. It is a category error and should be void as W1.2 evidence. On the actual software-QA record, displacement is BETTER corroborated by hard headcount than coding is (SOC 15-1253 −27% 2018→2023; manual-QA postings −25–40% from peak; FAANG deleted the STE title). The real reason NOT to over-bet W1.2 is the opposite of the Ford narrative: the labor IS displacing, but the VALUE is deflating — captured by free OSS (Playwright, where the hiring is), coding-agent self-testing (Qodo/Cursor/Claude Code), and incumbent Tricentis ($500M) — leaving no clean investable app-layer vendor. Consensus fears the agents can't test; the real risk is they can, and nobody owns the wedge.

name: Financial Reconciliation & Month-End Close
sw_tam: ~$1.1–1.5B close-automation category ARR (2026)
capture: ~0.4% (≈$1.2B category ARR ÷ ~$260B pool) if the whole close-automation category counts as capture; genuine coupled/agentic-displacement capture <0.1% — most ARR is additive tooling. The thesis is capture-EXPANSION, not the additive category revenue.
htc: Largely none on the core cell — enterprise close is incumbent/ERP-held (BlackLine $719M ARR+Verity, FloQast $200M+EY, SAP/Oracle/Workday embedding), and the AI-native challengers are already Series B/C at $1B+ (Rillet $1B, Basis $1.15B, FloQast $1.6B, Numeric ~$20M ARR) — seed door closed. Residual seed–A wedge (~$15–40M pre) only at (a) vertical/multi-entity/crypto/complex-consolidation close where incumbents are thin, or (b) the audit-trace-to-source certification layer bridging into W1.5 (officer-cert liability = ownable moat, not a wall).
falsi: By YE-2026: BlackLine hits its stated 25% platform (Verity agentic) ARR target AND May-2026 BLS OEWS shows bookkeeping/accounting/auditing clerks <1.34M (from 1.373M May-2025). By Q4-2027: agentic/"digital-worker" revenue >25% of the ~$1.2B close-automation category ARR (from <20% today). All three → Compression + capture-expansion confirmed. If platform ARR stalls <20% AND clerk headcount holds flat/up → category ARR is additive tooling; revert net to Mixed and cut conviction to Med.
anti: Consensus: AI-native startups (Rillet/Numeric/Basis) disrupt BlackLine and "month-end close gets automated away." Evidence-grounded contrarian read: (1) ~80%+ of the $1.2B close-software ARR is ADDITIVE workflow tooling that speeds the close without removing the controller — banking it as displacement repeats the ~10× coding error; (2) the SOX/officer-certification human is DURABLE (like coding's senior rung) → Expansion, so real compression is confined to the AP/reconciliation-clerk + staff-accountant rung (BLS clerks -6%/decade; AP -70–80%); (3) capture is genuinely CONTESTED, not clean startup-disruption — incumbents (BlackLine Verity, FloQast+EY, ERP-embedded close) are capturing the enterprise agentic transition while AI-native entrants re-platform the GL (Rillet) at the mid-market. Coupled displacement is real and production-proven at the clerk rung, but small, incumbent-tilted, and the seed door on the core cell is already closed.

name: Bookkeeping & SMB Accounting
sw_tam: ~$0.2–0.5B standalone AI-native bookkeeping ARR (unverified/blended); SMB mass-market value bundled into Intuit/Xero subscriptions, not separately monetized
capture: ≈0.2–0.4% of the displaced-labor pool (standalone startup ARR ~$0.3B / ~$150B, and much of that is human-service revenue; Intuit's embedded value deflates price rather than capturing wage)
htc: Largely NONE at the SMB mass-market tier — Intuit-captured (~82.5% share; Intuit Intelligence bundles done-for-you AI) and the firm-tier leaders (Basis $1.15B B, Digits ~$100M raised) are past seed. The only live seed/A wedge is the complex-vertical / firm-arbitrage layer QBO+Intuit-Assist can't reach: multi-entity consolidation, inventory/e-commerce & SaaS revenue-recognition, construction job-costing, nonprofit fund / crypto accounting, or agents sold INTO offshore (India/Philippines) outsourced-accounting firms (SA.3/SA.5 overlap). A seed/A check makes sense at ~$8–20M into a ≤$40–80M post on such a vertical; avoid another horizontal QBO-killer.
falsi: By the BLS OEWS May-2028 release, US SOC 43-3031 clerk employment falls below 1.40M (from ~1.50M in 2025) AND ≥1 standalone (non-Intuit/Xero) AI-bookkeeping vendor discloses ≥$100M VERIFIED ARR → incumbent-mediated compression confirmed with a live startup wedge. If clerk headcount holds ≥1.50M through 2028 → displacement stalled/falsified (books proved sticky-with-human). If NO standalone vendor clears $100M verified ARR by then → value capture is fully incumbent (Intuit-bundled) and the startup door is closed.
anti: Consensus: "AI kills bookkeepers → huge greenfield SaaS TAM for AI-bookkeeping startups." Anti-consensus: the wage bill is real and highly verifiable, but the value DEFLATES into Intuit/Xero (~82.5% SMB share) as a bundled feature — it defends the incumbent's subscription, it does not mint a standalone startup TAM. The durable startup wedge is NOT the SMB mass market (Intuit's fortress) but the accounting-FIRM / offshore-arbitrage tier (Basis, Truewind) — service-as-software where the buyer's OWN labor is what's displaced (SA.3/SA.5 overlap). And the compression is slow (BLS −6%/decade; Bench's fire-sale proves managed-service fragility), not a cliff. Underwrite as Intuit share-defense plus a narrow firm/vertical wedge — never as a QBO-killer landgrab.

name: Financial Reporting & Regulatory Filing (XBRL / trace-to-source)
labor_tam: $100-200B [W] — narrow high-comp slice: SEC/statutory-reporting staff (controllers, SEC-reporting managers, XBRL specialists) + external filing-agent labor, advanced-economy-weighted. Confirmed at frozen band.
sw_tam: ~$2-4B disclosure-management SW-TAM, incumbent-dominated (Workiva ~$800M+ rev, DFIN, Toppan Merrill); agent-specific slice small and being absorbed by incumbents, not a standalone software pool yet.
htc: Narrow — seed only if a pure-play trace-to-source / officer-certification-defensible filing agent emerges below Workiva/DFIN. But the incumbent-internalization falsifier the frozen hunt-list itself named is already triggering (DFIN AI-iXBRL Jun 2026, Workiva leading), so the window is closing. No investable pure-play pinned today.
falsi: By Q4 2027: if no VC-backed pure-play regulatory-filing/XBRL agent raises a Series A >$100M valuation while DFIN/Workiva ship AI-iXBRL at scale, incumbent capture is confirmed and the verdict locks to incumbent. Conversely a funded independent owning >10% of new AI-assisted SEC filings reopens the startup wedge.
anti: The frozen HTC hunt-list ranked W1.5 a top-3 open hunting ground (officer-cert liability = 'moat not wall'). I partially disagree: 2026 evidence shows the incumbents (DFIN AI-iXBRL Jun 2026, Workiva) internalizing the exact certification-defensible workflow that was supposed to be the startup moat — the falsifier the hunt-list named is already firing. The window is narrower than the frozen board implies.
players: Incumbents internalizing FAST in 2026: Workiva (disclosure-mgmt leader adding AI narrative-gen + XBRL), DFIN/Donnelley (AI-powered iXBRL tagging launched Jun 2026), Toppan Merrill; adjacent finance agents that could extend into filing: Basis, Ramp Accounting Agent, Digits; Focus Universal/Perfecular (micro-cap EDGARization+XBRL). No VC-backed pure-play regulatory-filing agent pinned — this is the white-space. No verified independent ARR.

name: Medical Coding & Revenue-Cycle Management
labor_tam: ~$90–130B (re-derived; frozen band was $100–150B — trim the top)
sw_tam: AI-native RCM agent ARR ~$0.5–1.5B realized 2026 (unverified), inside a $73–95B US RCM market ($180B global) being repriced to outcome/contingency
capture: ~0.3–0.6% (identifiable AI-native RCM ARR ÷ ~$90–130B pool) — above coding's 0.1–0.2%, below CX's 7–11%; the bet is capture-expansion off this low base.
htc: Coding core = essentially none — seed-closed. Autonomous-coding leaders (CodaMetrix Series C ~$164M raised, Fathom CVS-backed, Nym Epic-native) and the orchestration layer (Adonis Series C, Candid Series D, SmarterDx $1B PE) are all past the seed/A door. The live seed/A wedge (~$15–40M post) is the adjacent white-space the CMS-0057-F Jan-2027 API mandate opens: (a) prior-authorization automation — especially PAYER-side or specialty verticals (behavioral, dental, DME, ASC) where provider-side coding incumbents are weak; (b) denials/appeals orchestration for underserved mid-market/specialty practices. Underwrite to an INCUMBENT M&A exit (R1/Optum/Waystar/EHR), not standalone scale, given D=4 and the demonstrated absorption pattern; demand verified retained-ARR/NRR, not bookings or the $73–95B market headline.
falsi: By Q4-2027 (post CMS-0057-F prior-auth API go-live Jan 1 2027): does an INDEPENDENT autonomous-RCM startup (CodaMetrix/Fathom/Adonis/Candid) disclose ≥$150M verified ARR AND does BLS OES 29-2072 medical-records-specialist employment (base ~200,700) print a YoY decline in the May-2027 release? Both true → startup-capturable, shortage-masking is breaking, wage-bill compression is real (raise conviction). If instead Epic/R1/Optum bundle native autonomous coding as an attach and independents plateau or get acquired <$100M ARR while BLS headcount stays flat/up → incumbent capture + shortage absorbs the automation (lock Medium, treat as M&A-feeder, not category).
anti: Consensus: medical coders/billers are the poster-child of obviously-automatable white-collar work, so RCM is a slam-dunk displacement short. Two anti-consensus corrections: (1) The labor is dissolving INTO a ~30% certified-coder shortage — so for 2–3 years the realized effect is backlog-clearing + margin capture via non-replacement and offshore reabsorption, NOT visible layoffs; headcount stats will UNDERSTATE the wage-bill compression, and (like W1.8 SOC) the shortage gives political cover so the CX/BPO-style displacement backlash never materializes. (2) The market is right that the WORK automates and wrong that pure-play coding STARTUPS capture it: the value is being colonized by the EHR (Epic-native autonomous coding) and consolidated by services incumbents (R1/Optum), making this the clearest 'capability-real, capture-goes-to-incumbents' cell in the W1 finance cluster — the sharpest autonomous IP (Phare Health, Fathom, Pieces) is an M&A feeder, not an independent-scale category.

name: Structured Data Entry & Digital Back-Office
labor_tam: $300-500B [W] — mass-headcount global pool (data-entry clerks, back-office transaction processors). Confirmed at frozen band.
sw_tam: ~$6-10B: legacy RPA base (UiPath ~$1.5B rev, Automation Anywhere, Blue Prism) being disrupted/absorbed by computer-use-agent spend; the CUA layer is new SW spend riding on lab model APIs.
htc: None material — incumbent RPA (UiPath) + Microsoft own enterprise distribution and model labs own the computer-use capability (L=4); D=2 leaves no durable startup moat. Vertical single-app CUA point-solutions are possible but thin and easily commoditized.
falsi: OSWorld 2.0 long-horizon (multi-app, real-world) best-system score: crosses ~50% by Q4 2027 (from ~20% in 2026) -> back-office displacement accelerates and coupled capture rises materially; stays <30% -> long-horizon multi-app reliability remains the binding gate and displacement stays confined to bounded single-app tasks.
anti: The frozen conviction cited an 'OSWorld ~20% gate.' That gate has bifurcated: single-task OSWorld-Verified hit 67.1% (UiPath Screen Agent / Opus 4.5, Jan 2026) while OSWorld 2.0 long-horizon stays ~20%. The 'computer use is ready / RPA is dead' consensus is overstated — bounded single-app tasks cleared, but the long-horizon multi-app reliability real back-office work needs is still the binding constraint. I refined H 1->2 to reflect the single-task break; net stays Compression, conviction Medium.
players: UiPath (Screen Agent #1 on OSWorld-Verified at 67.1%, powered by Claude Opus 4.5, Jan 2026), Automation Anywhere, Microsoft (Power Automate + computer use), with Anthropic/OpenAI computer-use APIs as the underlying engine. Displacement is real but RPA/CUA revenue is SW spend, not coupled labor capture — no clean displacement ARR pinned.

name: Security Operations & Threat Triage (autonomous SOC)
sw_tam: ~$10–18B (2026 reported AI/autonomous-SOC software market; direction only) — pure-play agentic-SOC ARR undisclosed, est. <$300M combined, all unverified
htc: Seed/A in the ADJACENT white-space — NOT horizontal enterprise SOC triage. That core door is effectively closed: 7AI/Exaforce/Torq are A/B/D-funded and CrowdStrike/Palo Alto/Microsoft shipped bundled agentic triage at RSAC 2026 (feature-izing fast). Investable wedges where the incumbent EDR/SIEM-telemetry moat does NOT transfer: (a) OT/ICS-SOC (industrial, non-IT telemetry); (b) DFIR/incident-response & forensics automation; (c) agent-native mid-market/SMB MDR delivered as labor (the [L] backlog the platforms underserve); (d) the cross-telemetry / agent-behavioral-baseline gap VentureBeat flagged surviving all three incumbents — though that borders the [$] infra ledger, so keep it labor-denominated. Target seed–A at ~$10–40M post; underwrite a proprietary detection-telemetry moat + retained ARR, explicitly NOT deployment-spend velocity. Horizontal enterprise-SOC-analyst play = none (door closed / feature-ized).
falsi: By Q4 2027, resolve standalone-capture two ways: (BULL) at least one pure-play (7AI/Exaforce/Dropzone/Prophet) discloses ≥$100M verified ARR at >120% net revenue retention AND stays independent → durable standalone labor-capture. (BEAR / feature-ization — base case given RSAC-2026 shipping) the category is acquired into incumbents at <$1.5B (the NHI pattern: Astrix→Cisco, Oasis→Cyera), OR CrowdStrike/Palo Alto/Microsoft bundle autonomous triage into platform SKUs at ~zero incremental price → standalone capture collapses. Separately for the DISPLACEMENT sign: if BLS ISA employment growth decelerates below +5%/yr with the entry/tier-1 share falling → coupled compression confirmed; if the occupation keeps growing near +21%/decade → [L]-backlog expansion wins.
anti: Two anti-consensus reads against the 2026 "autonomous SOC replaces the analyst / solves the 3.4M shortage" headline. (1) The shortage is mostly an [L] latent-demand artifact nobody pays for — un-triaged backlog, not a paid wage bill — so it will NOT convert to displaced wages; the durable story is EXPANSION into never-serviced alerts while the occupation GROWS (+21% BLS), the opposite of "the SOC analyst is dead." (2) The value is tilting to INCUMBENTS, not the funded startups. RSAC 2026 already saw CrowdStrike Charlotte (trained on Falcon Complete analyst decisions — an EDR-telemetry moat a startup can't replicate), Palo Alto Cortex+Console, Microsoft Security Copilot and Cisco all ship agentic triage as first-party platform layers. The record startup rounds are deployment-spend velocity, not proof of durable standalone capture — the frozen falsifier ("incumbents ship autonomous triage as a feature") is already printing, and the NHI-consolidation outcome (acquired-out pre-maturity) is the base rate. Consensus crowns 7AI/Exaforce; the contrarian read is they are likely platform acquisition-fodder.

name: Retail Floor & Cashiering
labor_tam: $0.8-1.2T [W] confirmed (huge headcount, low comp-per-head — dollar-weighting strongly de-emphasizes this pool).
sw_tam: ~$1-3B cashierless/retail-vision + inventory-robot spend 2026 ([$], incumbent-dominated): Amazon Just Walk Out 360+ third-party sites (2x YoY); NCR/Toshiba self-checkout installed base; Simbe/Brain Corp inventory robots. Pure-play cashierless SW small/consolidating.
htc: None — incumbent-captured (Amazon JWO licensing, NCR/Toshiba self-checkout) and pure-play cashierless startups have largely stalled or been acquired; too-early on unit economics and last-10% CV accuracy. EU AI Act biometric limits (full applicability 2026) add regulatory drag.
falsi: Does Amazon JWO exceed ~700 third-party locations by end-2026 (from 360)? Does any grocery chain deploy full cashierless (not self-checkout) at >100 stores with published labor savings? If JWO stays airport/stadium-niche, mass retail displacement stays deferred.
anti: Consensus periodically declares 'cashiers are dead.' Reality: Amazon RETREATED from its own cashierless stores (2024, needed human labelers), self-checkout is being partially rolled back on shrink, and the pure-plays stalled. This is among the SLOWEST-converting large pools — low comp-per-head means low dollar-value even if displaced, and the tech keeps failing the last-10% accuracy wall. Dollar-weighting rightly de-emphasizes it.
players: Amazon Just Walk Out (pivoted to B2B licensing, 360+ airport/stadium sites; REMOVED from Amazon Fresh 2024 after 1,000+ India labelers — AI-washing cautionary tale); NCR/Toshiba (self-checkout incumbents); Simbe 'Tally' (Schnucks, SpartanNash); Brain Corp; Walmart/Symbotic (warehouse-adjacent). Pure-plays (Standard Cognition, Grabango, Trigo) stalled/consolidated.

name: Hospitality & Hotel Operations
labor_tam: $0.5-0.8T [W] confirmed (hotel-ops wage bill; large [L] tail from chronic understaffing). Housekeeping — the biggest labor line — is dexterous-physical and robot-hard, so coupled-capturable slice << pool.
sw_tam: ~$1-3B hotel-ops AI + robotics 2026: hospitality-robotics market ~$0.76-3.1B (delivery/reception robots) + voice-agent SW. Fragmented point solutions atop PMS incumbents (Oracle Opera, Cloudbeds).
htc: Thin — the seed-investable slice is front-desk/reservations VOICE agents (shortage tailwind = low displacement backlash, inverted social license), cross-ref W3.6; physical housekeeping too-early; PMS layer incumbent-owned. Underwrite retained ARR + named-chain rollouts, not robot-market TAM.
falsi: Does a hotel voice-agent vendor reach >$25-50M verified ARR with a named brand-chain rollout by end-2026? Does hotel-sector BLS employment decline against the shortage, or a housekeeping-robot deployment cross >100 properties? Absent these by mid-2027, this stays too-early.
anti: Both the displacement thesis AND the pool size are overstated near-term. The acute labor shortage means hotels ADOPT AI to fill unfillable roles, not cut heads → gap-filling/Expansion-flavored, not Compression. And the housekeeping bulk (biggest line) is dexterous-physical/robot-hard, so the $0.5-0.8T pool massively overstates 2026 coupled-capturable value. The only real 2026 story is thin voice-agent capture in a shortage — lowest conviction of the W10 set.
players: Voice agents (e.g. 'Annette' — cited handling up to 60% of front-desk calls / 87% call-center volume cut — vendor-reported, unverified); reception/delivery/housekeeping-corridor robots; PMS incumbents Oracle, Cloudbeds; BCG 'AI-first hotels' framing. Context: 65-87% of hotels reported staffing shortages 2025 (AHLA); 82% expanding AI use.

name: Food-Service Front-of-House & Ordering
labor_tam: $0.5-0.9T [W] confirmed (QSR front-of-house wage bill; low comp-per-head). Order-taking is a discrete, verifiable slice = cleaner coupling than retail floor.
sw_tam: ~$0.3-0.6B restaurant voice-AI ARR 2026, scaling fastest of the W10 set: SoundHound restaurant vertical (public, multi-vertical ~$150M+ total ARR), Presto (public, struggling), ConverseNow/Kea/PolyAI/Omilia. Production deployments real (Taco Bell ~900, Wendy's 500-600).
htc: Thin — drive-thru voice leaders are public (SoundHound, Presto) or big-tech/brand-owned (Google-Wendy's, McDonald's internal, Omilia late-stage). Seed room only in adjacent white-space: independent-restaurant phone ordering, agentic ordering for non-QSR, kitchen-ops.
falsi: Does drive-thru voice AI cross ~10% of US drive-thru locations (~20K+) by end-2026, from ~3-5K? Does a chain report FoH labor-hour reduction attributable to voice AI (vs reallocation to kitchen)? Watch for more rollbacks (McDonald's-IBM pattern) as the counter-signal.
anti: Voice ordering is the MOST production-real of the W10 cluster (Taco Bell 900, Wendy's 500+). But two hedges: (1) value accrues to public/incumbent vendors and brands building in-house, not seed startups — thin investable surface; (2) the labor effect is reallocation (order-taker → kitchen) more than net cut, so net-Mixed holds. Deployment momentum outruns the startup opportunity and the actual headcount displacement.
players: Taco Bell (Omilia, ~900 US restaurants); Wendy's FreshAI (Google Cloud, expanding to 500-600); White Castle (SoundHound 'Julia', ~100); Culver's/Zaxbys/Burger King live-or-piloting; McDonald's (ended IBM trial 2024, building internal). Vendors: SoundHound, Presto, ConverseNow, Kea, Hi Auto, PolyAI. ~3-5K locations live vs ~200K+ US drive-thrus → capture <1%.

name: Benefits/Case Processing & Citizen Service
sw_tam: ~$5–10B case/citizen-service agent deployment today (broad AI-in-gov ~$22B '24 → ~$98B '33, report-mill CAGR — directional only)
htc: none/thin — procurement moat + Palantir/ServiceNow/SI capture; capability is proven but sits inside gov-captive deployments. Only seed wedge: citizen-SIDE benefits-access navigators (consumer-sold, not gov-procured).
falsi: By Q4 2027, does a US state/federal agency auto-adjudicate >50% of a major benefit program via agents (à la Ireland MyWelfare 83%)? If still pilots, the US compression is procurement-blocked, not realized.
anti: Auto-award is ALREADY production-real abroad (Ireland 83% of illness claims) — the binding constraint is US procurement/politics, not capability. Consensus over-weights 'AI can't do gov work' and under-weights how fast non-US governments are already compressing caseworker headcount. But it is near-uninvestable for a US seed fund: value accrues to incumbents.
players: Incumbent-captured: Palantir & ServiceNow (public-sector workflow); Deloitte/Accenture SI delivery; Google Public Sector, Microsoft Copilot Gov. Production proof exists but is GOV-CAPTIVE, not vendor ARR: Ireland MyWelfare (83% illness / 98% treatment claims auto-awarded), Singapore GovTech single-portal benefits-matching, Buenos Aires (58M citizen interactions/yr).

name: Public Education Delivery
sw_tam: ~$7–8B global AI-education software '25 (US $2B '25 → $32.6B '34, report-mill); agent/tutor slice materially smaller
htc: none — R5 procurement + political + union protection; teacher headcount is politically protected, so this is Expansion/augment, not displacement. Any seed door is in supplemental/consumer tutoring, not public-sector seats.
falsi: By Dec 2027, does any US public district adopt AI-tutor-as-PRIMARY-instruction with a measured teacher-FTE reduction? If 100% augmentation persists, Expansion is locked and displacement ≈ 0.
anti: The 'AI will replace teachers' consensus is wrong-SIGNED here: public education is the cleanest Additive/Expansion case in the map — headcount is politically protected and a teacher shortage means AI backfills gaps, not seats. Huge labor TAM, but startup-capturable displacement value ≈ 0.
players: Google (Gemini for Education / LearnLM), OpenAI (ChatGPT Edu), Khan Academy (Khanmigo), MagicSchool AI, Third Space Learning, Microsoft Copilot. 86% of ed-orgs now use genAI (Microsoft — highest of any sector); Harvard RCT: well-designed AI tutor ~2× learning; teachers save ~5.9 hr/wk — all augmentation signals, not seat-elimination.

name: Public-Safety Records & Permitting
sw_tam: ~$2–4B permitting + public-safety-records software; PermitFlow $31M Series A, Flock Safety $658M total (most-funded GovTech, but surveillance/records HW)
htc: seed/A wedge in permitting & licensing automation (PermitFlow $31M A) — fragmented municipal buyers, low political heat vs benefits/police, less incumbent-locked. Public-safety records themselves are Axon/Palantir-captured (avoid).
falsi: By Q4 2027, does a top-20 US city reach >50% auto-issued permits (a PermitFlow-class deployment) and does Axon Draft One pass ~50% of US departments? Either signals real clerk compression vs pilot theater.
anti: Permitting is the one investable slice of an otherwise fully-blocked public sector — fragmented buyers, low political heat (clerks not cops), a real seed door (PermitFlow) that the 'public sector = all incumbent-captured' consensus misses. Kept Low overall, but the permitting wedge is a legitimate hunting ground.
players: PermitFlow ($31M A — permit prep/tracking, the genuine startup wedge), Axon Draft One (AI police-report drafting, in production across departments), Flock Safety ($658M total), Palantir/ServiceNow-gov, Truleo. Records/investigations mostly Axon/Palantir-captured.
